caveats: Requires the server to be configured with ProcessShellFactory/ProcessShellCommandFactory so an exec request creates a ProcessShell, and a channel close concurrent with exec startup (application-thread close, session disconnect/teardown, or remote CLOSE racing the request thread).
Fully serialized start-before-destroy destroys correctly; the leak needs destroy's null check to land before the process field is assigned (or destroy-first call order), not literally every ordering.
subclaims.reason: handleExec passes its isClosing guard (ChannelSession.java:578), creates a ProcessShell whose process is null via the factory (ChannelSession.java:603; ProcessShellCommandFactory.java:47-49; ProcessShellFactory.java:80-86), and sendResponse starts it with no closing check (ChannelSession.java:400). Close runs closeImmediately0, whose destroy no-ops when process is null (ProcessShell.java:176) and then nulls commandInstance (ChannelSession.java:217). If close interleaves after sendResponse passes its null check/dereference (ChannelSession.java:372/400) but before process = builder.start() (ProcessShell.java:119), destroy sees null while the OS process is then launched with its only reference dropped: a leak. No common lock or happens-before rules this out: commandInstance (ChannelSession.java:95) and process (ProcessShell.java:53) are plain fields with no synchronized/volatile anywhere on these paths, and the commandStarted AtomicBoolean (ChannelSession.java:96) only blocks double-start. The start side runs on the request-handling thread via handleInternalRequest to sendResponse (AbstractChannel.java:339-344); the destroy side runs on any thread closing the channel, e.g. remote CLOSE via handleClose (AbstractChannel.java:568-584), session disconnect, or an application thread calling the public close API.
